GUBERNATORIAL DISASTER PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS, beginning June 29, 2023, and continuing through July 4, 2023,
several rounds of severe storms passed through Illinois producing heavy rainfall, flash
flooding, hail, tornadoes, and straight-line winds threatening lives and causing
widespread damage and destruction to public and private property; and,
WHEREAS, on June 29th, central Illinois experienced a derecho that brought
damaging straight-line winds resulting in five (5) confirmed tornadoes, along with wind
gusts in excess of 100 miles per hour across multiple counties; and,
WHEREAS, the tornados and straight-line winds resulted in large debris fields,
affecting homeowners, businesses, utilities, and local governments; and,
WHEREAS, due to the significant number of downed trees, branches, and power
poles, widespread power outages to homes and businesses occurred; and,
WHEREAS, on June 30"h, a second wave of severe storms in southwest Illinois
produced damaging winds, hail, and rain resulting in additional widespread power
outages and a significant amount of debris across multiple counties; and,
WHEREAS, on July 2nd, a third set of severe storms dropped significant rainfall,
including localized totals of upwards of eight (8) inches of water, in a short period of
time, causing flash flooding in and around the Chicago area, including on the City's west
side in Austin and other communities; and,
WHEREAS, the July 2nd
storms also downed numerous trees and caused
widespread power outages in northern Illinois; and,
WHEREAS, the storms during this time period also caused disruptions to
transportation due to flash flooding and debris on the roadways; and,
WHEREAS, the continuation of severe storms throughout this time period caused
further damage to public and private property in the affected areas and inhibited the
ability of areas affected by previous storms to undertake effective response and recovery
operations; and,
WHEREAS, high temperatures and humidity throughout the entire period,
including during and after these storm systems, have required the opening of shelters and
public places in order to protect the public from heat-related injuries; and,
WHEREAS, as a result of these storms, the damage they caused to critical
infrastructure, and the ongoing danger and impacts to the public, extraordinary measures
are required, and have been implemented, to protect the health, safety, and welfare of the
people of Illinois; and,
WHEREAS, based on reports received by the Illinois Emergency Management
Agency and Office of Homeland Security, local resources and capabilities in the
---PAGE---
communities hit by these storms have been exhausted, and State resources are needed to
respond to and recover from the effects of the severe storms; and,
WHEREAS, these conditions provide legal justification under Section 7 of the
Illinois Emergency Management Act, 20 ILCS 3305/7, for the issuance of a proclamation
of disaster.
NOW, THEREFORE, in the interest of aiding the people of Illinois and the local
governments responsible for ensuring public health and safety, 1, JB Pritzker, Governor
of the State of Illinois, hereby proclaim as follows:
Section 1: Pursuant to the provisions of Section 7 of the Illinois Emergency
Management Agency Act, 20 ILCS 3305/7, I find that a disaster exists within the State of
Illinois and specifically declare Coles, Cook (including the City of Chicago), Edgar,
Hancock, McDonough, Morgan, Sangamon, and Washington Counties as disaster areas.
Section 2. The Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland
Security is directed to continue implementation of the State Emergency Operations Plan,
as it has been doing since June 29"h, and to coordinate State resources to support local
governments in disaster response and recovery operations.
To aid with emergency purchases necessary for response and othe
emergency powers as authorized by the Illinois Emergency Management Agency Act, the
provisions of the Illinois Procurement Code and the Illinois Joint Purchasing Act that
would in any way prevent, hinder or delay necessary action in coping with the disaster
are suspended to the extent they are not required by federal law.
This proclamation can facilitate a request for Federal disaster
assistance if a complete and comprehensive assessment of damage indicates that effective
recovery is beyond the capabilities of the State and affected local governments.
Section 5: This proclamation shall be effective immediately and remain in effect
for 30 days.

WHEREAS, on September 17, 2023, severe storms generating heavy rainfall moved
through Illinois; and
WHEREAS, according to the National Weather Service, these storms produced a range
of approximately three to nine inches of precipitation in some areas of the State; and
WHEREAS, this precipitation caused substantial flooding in communities located in
Cook County; and
WHEREAS, the flooding resulted in significant property damage to homes and
businesses, caused widespread power outages, impacted roads and transportation; and
WHEREAS, Cook County Proclaimed a Disaster on October 4, 2023 and requested aid
from the State, including preliminary damage assessments to facilitate state and federal
assistance; and
WHEREAS, requests for aid and the results of the preliminary damage assessments
made by the Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security indicate
that local resources and capabilities have been exhausted and that State resources are needed to
respond to and recover from the effects of the flooding; and
WHEREAS, these conditions provide legal justification under Section 7 of the Illinois
Emergency Management Agency Act for the issuance of a proclamation of disaster.
NOW, THEREFORE, in the interest of aiding the people of Illinois and the local
governments responsible for ensuring public health and safety, I, JB Pritzker, Governor of the
State of Illinois, hereby proclaim as follows:
Section 1: Pursuant to the provisions of Section 7 of the Illinois Emergency
Management Agency Act, 20 ILCS 3305/7, I find that a disaster exists within the State of Illinois
and specifically declare Cook County a disaster area.
Section 2. The Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland
Security is directed to continue implementation of the State Emergency Operations Plan, as it has
been doing since September 17, 2023, and to coordinate State resources to support local
governments in disaster response and recovery operations.
Section 3. To aid with emergency purchases necessary for response and other
emergency powers as authorized by the Illinois Emergency Management Agency Act, the
provisions of the Illinois Procurement Code and the Illinois Joint Purchasing Act that would in
any way prevent, hinder or delay necessary action in coping with the disaster are suspended to
---PAGE---
the extent they are not required by federal law. If necessary, and in accordance with Section 7(1)
of the Illinois Emergency Management Agency Act, 20 ILCS 3305/7(1), the Governor may take
appropriate executive action to suspend additional statutes, orders, rules, and regulations.
Section 4: This proclamation can facilitate a request for Federal disaster assistance if a
complete and comprehensive assessment of damage indicates that effective recovery is beyond
the capabilities of the State and affected local governments.
Section 5:
This proclamation shall be effective immediately and remain in effect for 30
days.

and recovering from the effects of this disaster including protecting public health and
safety and lessening or averting the threats of more severe and lasting harm; and,
HEREAS, these conditions provide legal justification under section 7 of t
inois Emergency Management Agency Act tor the issuance ot a proclamation
disaster.
NOW, THEREFORE, I, JB Pritzker, Governor of the State of Illinois, pursuant to
the executive authority vested in me by the Illinois Constitution and laws, and in the
interest of aiding the people of Illinois and the local governments responsible for
ensuring public health and safety, hereby proclaim as follows:
Section 1: Pursuant to the provisions of Section 7 of the Illinois Emergency
Management Agency Act, 20 ILCS 3305/7, I find that a disaster exists within the State of
Illinois and specifically declare each of these counties a disaster area:
Alexander,
Champaign, Cook, DuPage, Ford, Fulton, Kane, LaSalle, Lake, McLean, Marshall,
Pulaski, Tazewell, Vermilion, and Will.
ection 2: LEMA-UHS 15 directed to continue implementation of the sta
mergency Uperations Plan and coordinate state resources to support local governmen
in disaster response and recovery operations.
Section 3: The linois Department of Transportation, linois Environmental
Protection Agency, and Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity
shall assist local governments with response and recovery efforts as appropriate. All other
State agencies are directed to collaborate with IEMA-OHS to identify and enable
capabilities for disaster response and recovery activities.
Section 4: To aid with emergency purchases necessary for response and other
emergency powers as authorized by the Illinois Emergency Management Agency Act, the
provisions of the Illinois Procurement Code, Joint Purchasing Act, and State Property
Control Act that would in any way prevent, hinder or delay necessary action in coping
with the disaster are suspended to the extent they are not required by federal law.
To aid with disposal of debris caused by these severe storms,
including but not limited to the use of incineration devices, all statutory and regulatory
provisions that require permitting or licensing that in any way prevent, hinder or dela!
necessary action in coping with the disaster are suspended to the extent they are no
required by federal law.
Section 6: This proclamation can facilitate requests for federal and State disaster
for 30 days.
